<!-- ============================== HERO ============================== -->
<header class="section hero" id="top">
  <span class="kicker">SCPU3001 · Industry partner: ANSTO</span>
  <h1>Licensing<br>Synroc</h1>
  <p class="lede">Making the parent of the most used nuclear-medicine isotope leaves radioactive waste behind, and ANSTO's Synroc can shrink it by up to 99%. Our question: <b>where, and in what form, should ANSTO offer Synroc abroad?</b></p>
  <div class="hero-actions">
    <a class="cta solid" href="#decision">Try the decision model</a>
    <a class="cta" href="#newCountry">Score a new country</a>
  </div>
  <div class="grid-4">
    <div class="panel stat reveal"><div class="num" data-count="99" data-suffix="%">99%</div><div class="lab">less waste volume than cement, at best <a class="cite" href="references.html#r2">[2]</a></div></div>
    <div class="panel stat reveal"><div class="num"><span data-count="2">2</span> sites</div><div class="lab">of 6 candidates pass the screen: Petten (NL) and Fleurus (BE)</div></div>
    <div class="panel stat reveal"><div class="num" data-count="100" data-suffix="%">100%</div><div class="lab">of 10,000 weightings rank the Netherlands first</div></div>
    <div class="panel stat reveal"><div class="num"><span data-count="3">3</span> gates</div><div class="lab">to pass before any licence is signed</div></div>
  </div>
  <p class="team-line">Morris · Lydia · Ibrahim · Andres · Tommy · Delphine — University of Sydney, November 2026</p>
</header>

<!-- ============================ PROBLEM ============================= -->
<section class="section" id="problem">
  <span class="kicker">01 · The problem</span>
  <h2>A proven fix,<br>an unknown market</h2>
  <p class="lede">Making molybdenum-99 (Mo-99) leaves 2.6–15 m³ of liquid radioactive waste a year worldwide <a class="cite" href="references.html#r1">[1]</a>, <a class="cite" href="references.html#r3">[3]</a>. Cemented, it grows about 25-fold and is stored for decades until a repository opens <a class="cite" href="references.html#r4">[4]</a>. ANSTO's Synroc shrinks it instead, and its first plant, SyMo, is being commissioned <a class="cite" href="references.html#r5">[5]</a>. What ANSTO lacks is an evidence-based way to decide <b>where</b> to offer it.</p>
  <div class="grid-2" style="margin-top:28px">
    <div class="panel reveal">
      <h3>Shrink the waste</h3>
      <p class="note" style="margin-top:0">Drag to set the liquid waste a producer makes each year. Cube sizes are drawn to true volume.</p>
      <div class="control">
        <label for="vol">Liquid waste per year <output id="volOut">3.0 m³</output></label>
        <input type="range" id="vol" min="0.5" max="15" step="0.1" value="3">
      </div>
      <svg class="cubes" id="cubes" viewBox="0 0 560 300" role="img" aria-label="Volume comparison cubes"></svg>
    </div>
    <div class="panel reveal">
      <h3>What changes</h3>
      <div class="big-compare">
        <span class="pill pink">Cemented: <b id="cemOut">25 m³</b></span>
        <span class="pill mint">Synroc: <b id="synOut">0.25–1 m³</b></span>
      </div>
      <p style="margin-top:18px">Cemented, each cubic metre becomes about <b>25 m³</b> of packages that must be stored, and paid for, until disposal. Synroc turns it into <b>0.25–1 m³</b> of dense ceramic <a class="cite" href="references.html#r2">[2]</a>, <a class="cite" href="references.html#r3">[3]</a>.</p>
      <p><b>Our aim:</b> give ANSTO an evidence-based answer, and a reusable tool, for where and in what commercial form to offer Synroc abroad.</p>
      <h3 style="margin-top:22px">Who decides whether it works</h3>
      <div class="grid-2" style="gap:10px">
        <div class="pill mint">Waste owners: does it save money?</div>
        <div class="pill blue">Regulators: can it be licensed?</div>
        <div class="pill" style="background:var(--lilac)">Scientists: does the waste match?</div>
        <div class="pill pink">Host towns: will they accept it?</div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="panel reveal" style="margin-top:22px">
    <h3>Why ANSTO cannot just pick a country</h3>
    <p style="margin-top:0">A market exists only where all four conditions hold at once. Judged on any one alone, the obvious first market changes:</p>
    <div class="grid-4" style="gap:12px">
      <div class="pill blue"><b>Biggest inventory</b> → Canada</div>
      <div class="pill" style="background:var(--lilac)"><b>Readiest regulator</b> → United Kingdom</div>
      <div class="pill mint"><b>Matching chemistry</b> → every fission Mo-99 producer</div>
      <div class="pill pink"><b>Future supply</b> → France</div>
    </div>
    <p style="margin-bottom:0">So we did not start from the Netherlands and Belgium. We started from six candidates, tested every one on all four conditions, and let the evidence choose. The two European sites are <b>the result</b> of the screen, not its starting point, and the same tool can re-test any country as evidence changes.</p>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ============================= WHERE ============================== -->
<section class="section" id="where">
  <span class="kicker">02 · Where the waste is</span>
  <h2>Six candidates, each a plausible first market</h2>
  <p class="lede">We searched the Commonwealth and the EU because their rules differ: the EU has a binding waste directive <a class="cite" href="references.html#r23">[23]</a>; the Commonwealth has none. Inside them we took every fission Mo-99 producer, plus each country a one-condition search would have picked, the EU's shared rules, and Australia as benchmark. Cases likely to fail were included on purpose: a screen that passed everyone would prove nothing, and each exclusion tells ANSTO where not to spend effort. Click a country.</p>
  <div class="legend">
    <span><i class="st-Proceeds"></i>Proceeds to ranking</span>
    <span><i class="st-Evidence"></i>Evidence gap</span>
    <span><i class="st-Benchmark"></i>Benchmark or legal baseline</span>
    <span><i class="st-Excluded"></i>Excluded or revisit later</span>
  </div>
  <div class="chips" id="chips"></div>
  <div class="panel detail reveal" id="countryDetail"></div>
  <p class="note">No jurisdiction legally blocks Synroc. Legal score: how clear the licensing pathway is. Political score: Kingdon's policy-window model <a class="cite" href="references.html#r7">[7]</a>. Both 1–5.</p>
</section>

<!-- =========================== QUESTIONS ============================ -->
<section class="section" id="questions">
  <span class="kicker">03 · Four questions</span>
  <h2>Four questions, one decision</h2>
  <p class="lede">Every candidate faces the same four questions, one per condition a market must meet. Three answers can rule a country out at once (no matching waste, a legal block, too little waste to pay); the rest become scores in the decision tool.</p>
  <div class="tabs" id="rqTabs"></div>
  <div class="rq-grid" id="rqPanel"></div>
</section>

<!-- ============================ DECISION ============================ -->
<section class="section" id="decision">
  <span class="kicker">04 · The decision model</span>
  <h2>A decision tool ANSTO can reuse</h2>
  <p class="lede">Four scores in, a recommendation out. Stage 1 screens out any country that fails a must-have. Stage 2 ranks the rest with weights <a class="cite" href="references.html#r6">[6]</a>. Set your own priorities, then score a new country below to see where it would rank.</p>
  <div class="grid-2" style="margin-top:26px">
    <div class="panel reveal">
      <h3>Your weights</h3>
      <div class="seg presets" id="presets">
        <button data-w="25,25,25,25" class="on">Equal</button>
        <button data-w="15,55,15,15">Cost</button>
        <button data-w="15,15,15,55">Community</button>
        <button data-w="55,15,15,15">Technology</button>
      </div>
      <div id="weightControls"></div>
      <p class="wsum" id="wsum"></p>
    </div>
    <div class="panel reveal">
      <h3>Who ranks first</h3>
      <div class="bars" id="rankBars"></div>
      <div class="verdict" id="verdict"></div>
      <p class="note" id="smaaNote"></p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="panel reveal" id="whyNL" style="margin-top:22px">
    <span class="kicker">The statistics</span>
    <h3>Why the Netherlands ranks first, and how we tested it</h3>
    <div class="grid-2" style="margin-top:14px">
      <div>
        <p style="margin-top:0"><b>1 · It is never worse.</b> The Netherlands scores 3, 5, 4 and 3 on the technical, economic, law-and-politics and social criteria; Belgium scores 2, 4, 3.5 and 3. With weights <i>w</i> summing to one, the gap is</p>
        <p style="text-align:center;font-size:18px;margin:6px 0 10px">V(NL) − V(BE) = <i>w</i><sub>tech</sub> + <i>w</i><sub>econ</sub> + 0.5 <i>w</i><sub>law</sub></p>
        <p>This is above zero for every weighting except one that puts all weight on social licence, where the two tie. In MCDA terms, the Netherlands <b>dominates</b> Belgium <a class="cite" href="references.html#r6">[6]</a>.</p>
        <p><b>2 · Random weights (SMAA-2).</b> ANSTO has not set weights, so we drew 10,000 random sets, every combination equally likely, and recorded who ranked first <a class="cite" href="references.html#r11">[11]</a>. The chart shows the gap in every draw: all are above zero.</p>
        <p><b>3 · Uncertain scores.</b> Scores are judgements, so we also let every score move by up to half a point, then a full point, in 10,000 more draws each.</p>
        <p style="margin-bottom:0"><b>4 · The one weak point.</b> The ranking does not depend on preferences, but it does depend on one fact: Petten's waste volume, which is estimated at 0.7 m³ a year. Measuring it is the first task.</p>
      </div>
      <div>
        <svg class="econ-svg" id="gapSvg" viewBox="0 0 560 200" role="img" aria-label="Histogram of the Netherlands' score minus Belgium's across 10,000 random weightings"></svg>
        <div class="kpis" style="margin-top:6px">
          <div class="kpi"><div class="v" id="rbSmaa"></div><div class="l">of 10,000 weightings rank NL first (median gap <span id="rbMed"></span>)</div></div>
          <div class="kpi"><div class="v" id="rbHalf"></div><div class="l">still first if every score is ±0.5 out</div></div>
          <div class="kpi"><div class="v" id="rbOne"></div><div class="l">still first if every score is ±1 out</div></div>
        </div>
        <p class="note">Robust means first in at least <span id="rbThr"></span> of draws, a threshold set before the analysis. Volume: the Dutch stream fails the screen after a <b id="rbVol"></b> fall, against <span id="rbVolBE"></span> for Belgium's documented stream. Computed in R when the site is built (seed 2026); full method in the report, Section 3.7 and Appendix B.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="panel newc reveal" id="newCountry">
    <div class="newc-head">
      <div>
        <span class="kicker">Reusable framework</span>
        <h3>Score a new country</h3>
        <p class="note" style="margin-top:4px">Enter four scores from 1 (poor) to 5 (strong) and tick the must-haves. The tool ranks the country against the Netherlands and Belgium using the weights above. Everything runs in your browser: nothing you enter is sent or saved, so ANSTO can test confidential producer data here.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="seg" id="ncExamples">
        <button data-ex="za">Example: South Africa</button>
        <button data-ex="fr">Example: France</button>
        <button data-ex="blank">Reset</button>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="grid-2">
      <div>
        <div class="control"><label for="ncName">Country name</label>
          <input type="text" id="ncName" class="text-in" value="New country" maxlength="40" autocomplete="off"></div>
        <div id="ncSliders"></div>
        <fieldset class="musts">
          <legend>Must-haves (Stage 1 screen)</legend>
          <label><input type="checkbox" id="ncM1" checked> Has liquid waste from fission Mo-99</label>
          <label><input type="checkbox" id="ncM2" checked> No legal block on a treatment plant, new technology or foreign technology</label>
          <label><input type="checkbox" id="ncM3" checked> Volume above the licensing break-even (about 0.5–1 m³ a year)</label>
        </fieldset>
      </div>
      <div>
        <h3>Where it would rank</h3>
        <div class="bars" id="ncBars"></div>
        <div class="verdict" id="ncVerdict"></div>
        <p class="note" id="ncRobust"></p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ============================ ECONOMICS =========================== -->
<section class="section" id="economics">
  <span class="kicker">05 · The economics</span>
  <h2>Timing, not chemistry, decides</h2>
  <p class="lede">Where the waste agency charges for disposal at hand-over, every cubic metre avoided saves the full charge. Where disposal is decades away, discounting erases the saving.</p>
  <div class="grid-2" style="margin-top:26px">
    <div class="panel reveal">
      <h3>Does licensing pay?</h3>
      <div class="seg" id="econCountry"></div>
      <div class="control">
        <label for="econVol">Producer's liquid waste <output id="econVolOut"></output></label>
        <input type="range" id="econVol" min="0.1" max="5" step="0.1" value="0.7">
      </div>
      <svg class="econ-svg" id="econSvg" viewBox="0 0 560 150" role="img" aria-label="Volume against break-even"></svg>
      <div class="kpis">
        <div class="kpi"><div class="v" id="kSave"></div><div class="l">median saving per m³ (modelled volume)</div></div>
        <div class="kpi"><div class="v" id="kHead"></div><div class="l">volume it can lose and still pay</div></div>
        <div class="kpi"><div class="v" id="kP"></div><div class="l">of 20,000 scenarios cheaper than cement (at the modelled volume)</div></div>
      </div>
      <p class="note">Median saving per m³ and break-even volumes from our 20,000-draw Monte Carlo model; present values at a 3.5% real discount rate <a class="cite" href="references.html#r10">[10]</a>.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="panel reveal">
      <h3>Why distance kills value</h3>
      <div class="control">
        <label for="years">Years until the disposal charge is paid <output id="yearsOut"></output></label>
        <input type="range" id="years" min="0" max="60" step="1" value="0">
      </div>
      <svg class="econ-svg" id="pvSvg" viewBox="0 0 560 230" role="img" aria-label="Present value of A$1 avoided"></svg>
      <p id="pvText" style="margin-top:10px"></p>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- ============================== RISKS ============================= -->
<section class="section" id="risks">
  <span class="kicker">06 · What could go wrong</span>
  <h2>Sixteen risks, three that could stop everything</h2>
  <p class="lede">Agency refusal (R1), no operating licence for SyMo (R6) and a formulation that fails on real waste (R7) would remove both countries at once. They cannot be diversified, so each becomes a gate. Ratings follow ISO 31000; the full register is in the report, Appendix A.</p>
  <div class="seg" id="riskMode" style="margin:18px 0 18px">
    <button class="on" data-m="inherent">Before treatment</button>
    <button data-m="residual">After treatment</button>
  </div>
  <div class="grid-2">
    <div class="panel reveal">
      <div class="matrix-wrap">
        <div class="axis-y">Likelihood →</div>
        <div class="matrix" id="matrix"></div>
      </div>
      <div class="axis-x"><span>Low impact</span><span>Medium</span><span>High impact</span></div>
    </div>
    <div class="panel risk-detail reveal" id="riskDetail"></div>
  </div>
</section>

<!-- =============================== PLAN ============================= -->
<section class="section" id="plan">
  <span class="kicker">07 · Our plan</span>
  <h2>Our recommendation</h2>
  <p class="lede">We recommend licensing Synroc to COVRA (Netherlands) first and ONDRAF (Belgium) in parallel, each priced on the disposal cost the agency avoids, with no licence signed until three gates are passed. Click a step.</p>
  <div class="stepper" id="stepper"></div>
  <div class="panel reveal" id="stepDetail"></div>
  <h3 style="margin-top:44px">How ANSTO engages the Netherlands and Belgium</h3>
  <div class="asks">
    <div class="ask"><b>Government first.</b> Brief DFAT and use the Australia–Euratom nuclear cooperation agreement to open talks in The Hague and Brussels.</div>
    <div class="ask"><b>Waste agencies.</b> Propose joint waste characterisation and Synroc tests with COVRA and ONDRAF.</div>
    <div class="ask"><b>Producers and regulators.</b> Confirm volumes with Curium and IRE (Petten's has never been published); brief ANVS and FANC early.</div>
    <div class="ask"><b>Communities.</b> Each licensee consults its host community (Petten or Nieuwdorp, Fleurus or Dessel) before any contract.</div>
  </div>
  <p class="note"><b>Limitations.</b> Public documents only; no interviews with COVRA, ONDRAF or the producers. The Dutch volume is estimated. TRL 6 is provisional. Social licence evidence cannot yet compare sites. The eight cases test the framework rather than cover every country; producers outside the two blocs were not assessed, but the tool can screen them.</p>
</section>
